The structure and activities of S is described below:
Structure of the cerebrum: The forebrain or the cerebrum is the most anterior division of the developing vertebrate brain, containing the most complex networks in the central nervous system. The forebrain has two major divisions: the diencephalon and the telencephalon.
The diencephalon is lower, containing the thalamus and hypothalamus (which together form the limbic system); the telencephalon is on top of the diencephalon and contains the cerebrum, the home of the highest-level cognitive processing in the brain. It is the large and complicated forebrain that distinguishes the human brain from other vertebrate brains.
Activities of the cerebrum: Forebrain is the higher organ which receives nerve impulses and sends responses to the various organs of the body. Cerebrum is the centre for body movement i.e., for every activity and sensation. Conscious activities of voluntary muscles are controlled by the cerebrum. It also helps in taking decisions and in responding to stimulation."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the functions of 'T' mentioned in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The 'T' in the stem refers to spinal cord. Spinal cord controls the reflex action. A reflex action is a sudden response or automatic reaction. The action can be described using an example:
If needle picks a hand unintentionally, the hand moves away. This is the result of a reflex reaction. At the time of picking, the dendrites of the sensory neuron, the skin accepts the stimulus and the stimulus transmits from the finger to the grey matter of the spinal cord through axon of the neuron. Impulse is transmitted from axon of the secondary neuron located at the grey matter of the spinal cord to the dendrite of the motor nerve by electrochemical process. So, impulse from the dendrite ultimately reaches the muscle and muscle contracts and the hand is moved away.

question: Sadia has made the hand note by her writing as the part of preparation for honours final exam. Her mother told her to take care of cooking. After hearing the sound, she entered into the kitchen and held up the hot lid of aluminium and kept off from her hand. As a result, her mother became angry.
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called hormone?","marks":1,"answer":"Hormones are the ductless secretions from the human body and animals that control various physiological functions of the body."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why the movement of diatom is called universal movement?","marks":2,"answer":"When a part of the plant body moves from one place to another as a whole, it is called universal movement. Universal movement is seen in unicellular algae named diatom."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the mechanism of special process that was occurred in the kitchen of Sadia.","marks":3,"answer":"The sudden keep off aluminum hot lid from Sadia's hand is accomplished mainly by reflex action, which means sudden response or automatic reaction. It caused by the spinal cord, not the brain. Events of hot lid keep off from hand reflex action happen consecutively in the following ways:
Skin contains sensory neurons. When a hot lid is lifted, the stimuli is accepted by the dendrites of the sensory neuron where skin acts as the receptor. This stimulus is transmitted through the synapses and reaches the gray matter of the brain through the spinal cord. This step is carried out by an electrochemical process where the motor neurons receive the stimuli from the sensory neurons through synapse. Then, the motor neurons transmit impulses to the muscle and the muscle contract accordingly to the command of the central nervous system. As a result, Sadia kept off the hot lid from her hand."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"An organ of human body performs special role in the activities of exam preparation of Sadia. Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"According to the stem, brain' is the organ of human body that performs special role in the activities of exam preparation of Sadia. It is analyzed below:
12 pairs of nerves emerge from the brain and 31 pairs from the spinal cord in the human body and branch out that spread throughout the body. These nerves carry all the sensations from different parts of the body to the brain. As Sadia prepared her handnotes, the light from the notebook stimulated the retinas of her eyes, causing nerve impulses. These impulses travels through the optic nerve to the visual center of the brain. From there, these impulses reach the voluntary muscles of Sadia's hand via the motor nerves through thought centers, memory centers, etc. Then Sadia started writing with her hand on that instruction. Thus the excitatory action of Sadia occurs by conducting the stimulus. If the brain did not receive that light stimulus, the muscles of Sadia's hand would not get any instructions. As a result, Sadia's exam preparation activities were disrupted. So it can be said that the brain of the human body plays a very important role by stimulating the muscles of the hand in the process of preparing for the exam.
---"}]

The brain is divided into three main parts:
Forebrain or prosencephalon: The largest part of the brain is cerebrum which consists of two incompletely divided lobes, the right and the left lobes. They are separated by deep furrows. These are cerebral hemispheres. The right hemisphere controls the left side of the body and the left hemisphere controls the right side of the body.
Midbrain or mesencephalon: The upper part of the hindbrain is midbrain or mesencephalon. It is a bridge between forebrain and hindbrain.
Hindbrain or rhombencephalon: It consists of cerebellum, pons and medulla oblongata. Cerebellum is located at the back part of pons. If its activity is hindered, then some physical problems may arise.
Numerous neuron cells combine together to form the nervous system. The nervous tissue plays an important role in keeping the body healthy and normal by properly directing different activities of the human body. The nervous system generally controls and coordinates the activities of different body organs. Any movement, or contraction, and expansion of hands and legs, movement of the mouth etc. are directly regulated by the neurons. Besides that, the nervous tissue receives stimulus from the environment and make necessary responses and implement them. Nerve cells also co-ordinate the activities of the different organs. As a result balance of the body is maintained. So, from the above discussion, it becomes clear that if the above neuron cells are absent or injured in the human body then the body will lose the coordination of activities of different organs and the balance of the human body will not be established. Man will fail to move and walk, will not be able to take his own food and fail to take any decision and will have no memory. In one word, the human body will be converted into a non-living substance if the nerve cells are injured or absent.
So, these are the problems that may arise if the neurons are damaged.

This sudden response is known as reflex action.
Reflex action means a sudden response or automatic reaction. Suddenly a needle pricks in the hand or on touching a hot object we immediately turn off hand from the source of stimulation. This is the result of reflex action. We cannot control the reflex action according to the will. Basically, it is controlled by the spinal cord, not by the brain. That is the immediate response to a specific stimulus is not controlled by the spinal cord instead of the brain is called reflex action. For example, a needle prick in the hand while sewing in an unconscious way or carelessly may cause a sudden jerking away of the hand. That is a reflex action. The events in such a reflex action are described in this way. At the time of pricking the dendrites of the sensory neuron, skin accepts the stimulus. Skin acts as a receptor. This stimulus transmits from the finger to the grey matter of the spinal cord through the axon of the neuron. It is the motor or efferent neurons which transmit impulses from the spinal cord to the dendrite of motor neuron. Here impulse is transmitted from the axon of the sensory neuron located at the grey matter of the spinal cord to the dendrite of the motor nerve by electrochemical process. Impulse transmits between the axon of the sensory nerve and dendrite of the motor or efferent nerve through the synapse. Then, the impulse from the dendrite impulse ultimately reaches the muscles and the muscles contract according to the command of the central nervous system. So, the hand is turned off from the source of stimulation automatically. Thus, sudden response is controlled by the spinal cord.

In the human body, muscle tissue performs various physical tasks. Through the contraction and relaxation of muscle cells, different organs in the body are moved, enabling locomotion and internal transportation. Voluntary muscle contraction and relaxation allow movement of limbs like arms and legs. Muscles play an important role in human movement. Voluntary muscles are connected to bones by strong and elastic tendons. When nerve impulses stimulate the muscles, they contract. When the stimulus is removed, the muscles relax again. This contraction and relaxation of muscles enable movement of adjacent bones. In this way, muscles move parts of the body away from or toward the body axis. They lift certain parts and lower others, thereby facilitating human movement. Involuntary muscles primarily aid in the movement of internal organs (e.g., the peristaltic contractions of the intestines during digestion). From a special stage in fetal development to the moment just before death, the heart muscles contract and relax at a steady pace to keep blood circulating in the body. The structure and function of various endocrine glands are described below:
- Pituitary Gland: Located at the base of the brain. Secretes gonadotropic, somatotropic, TSH, ACTH. Primary hormone-producing gland.
- Thyroid Gland: Located in the neck, above the trachea. Secretes thyroxine. Aids in growth, metabolism, and reproductive organ development.
- Parathyroid Glands: Four glands located behind the thyroid. Secrete parathormone. Regulates calcium and phosphorus metabolism.
- Thymus Gland: Located in the neck region. Secretes thymosin. Aids in reproductive organ development.
- Adrenal Glands: Located above the kidneys. Secrete adrenaline. Helps relieve intense mental stress.
- Islets of Langerhans: Located within the pancreas. Secretes insulin and glucagon. Regulates blood glucose levels.
- Gonads: Ovaries in females, testes in males. Secrete estrogen and progesterone. Regulate reproductive organ growth, cycles, and sexual behavior.

Any of various hormones produced by plants that controls or regulates germination, growth, metabolism, or other physiological activities is called phytohormone. Its role is analyzed below:
Every plant cell is capable of producing hormones. They are produced in small quantities and regulate various biological functions. Florigen hormone in plants helps in flowering. Under the influence of auxin hormone, roots grow from grafted buds, preventing fruits from shedding prematurely, the rate of osmosis and respiration increases. The gibberellin hormone increases the length of the plant's internodes, which helps plants grow excessively. If this hormone is applied to stunted plants, the plant will grow taller than other normal plants. Besides, it plays an effective role in blooming flowers, shortening the duration of seed dormancy and germination. Cytokinin hormones can be mixed with auxin in varying proportions to stimulate cell division. Besides, it plays a role in cell growth, organ or parts of plants development, breaking the dormancy of seeds and organs, and delaying the aging process. During cell division, cytokinesis of cells occurs under the influence of cytokinin hormone. Therefore, this is how phytohormones promote plant growth and development."}]

At the primary stage of the disease, it begins with tremor of hands and legs. Tremor of eye lids is observed. Stiffness in the face, pain in muscles, feels trouble in movement, such as feeling uneasiness at the time of standing or while starts walking. Facial muscles do not move accordingly while talking."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How will the system of above figure give response against bite of mosquito?","marks":3,"answer":"A reflex action is a way for the body to automatically and rapidly respond to a stimulus to minimize any further damage to the body. In the stem, an example of reflex action in human beings has been depicted. So, at the time of pricking the dendrites of the sensory neuron, the skin accepts the stimulus. The skin acts as a receptor.
This stimulus transmits from the finger to the grey matter of the spinal cord through the axon of the neuron. The relay neurons transmit impulses from the spinal cord to the dendrite of motor neuron. Here impulse is transmitted from the axon of the sensory neuron located at the grey matter of the spinal cord to the dendrite of the motor nerve by electro chemical process resulting in a synapse. So, the impulse from the dendrites ultimately reaches the muscle and the muscle contracts according to the command of the central nervous system. So, the hand moves away from the source of the stimulation automatically.
Therefore, this is how reflex action works."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Describe the mechanism of transmission of pain of mosquito bite through the system of above figure.","marks":4,"answer":"In the stem, the process that is depicted is known as reflex action. Reflex action is an involuntary and instantaneous movement in response to a stimulus. This action is generally controlled by the spinal cord, not involving the brain.
Stimulus → receptor → sensory neuron → relay neuron → motor neuron → effector → response
According to the stem, receptor in the skin detects a stimulus of the sensation of a mosquito bite on the skin. Sensory neuron sends impulses to relay neuron through axon. Motor neuron sends impulses to effector neuron which is caused by a synapse between axon of sensory neuron and dendrite of motor neuron. Effector produces a response, such as muscle contraction and expansion to direct the hand where the mosquito is which occurs according to the command of central nervous system. As a result, the hands move away on their own.
---"}]

The Brain is divided into three parts:

Cerebrum is the centre for body movement i.e., for every activity and sensation. Conscious activities, e.g. speech, vision, hearing, intelligence, memory, thinking, will and activities of voluntary muscles are controlled by the cerebrum. It also helps in taking decisions and in responding to stimulation. A reflex action is a sudden response or automatic reaction. The brain, composed of the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain, plays a crucial role in maintaining healthy living by controlling all bodily functions. The forebrain is the largest part of brain. It includes the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus. They are essential for complex cognitive activities, sensory processing, and regulating emotions. An analytical discussion about stroke is given below:
A stroke is when the activity of the nervous system is hampered due to lack of blood supply to the brain. A stroke happens in the brain, not in heart, though there is a misconception about it. A stroke can happen either by brain hemorrhage or blood clotting in the brain. In both cases it obstructs blood supply to the brain. Generally, high blood pressure is the cause of brain hemorrhage. The symptoms of stroke are: vomiting, severe headache, a patient becomes unconscious within a few minutes, shoulder may be hard, muscles relax, respiration and pulse rate decrease, face turns red. Sometimes without any acute symptoms only face may be shapeless or patient may be fainted for a little time due to stroke. To measure the level of severity of a stroke, patients should be kept under observation. It may be ensured by detecting if there is any blood clotting or brain hemorrhage. In many cases the exact cause of the stroke cannot be ascertained. It is not possible to stop bleeding in the case of hemorrhage. Measures should be taken to keep high blood pressure under control. Surgical operations can also be done. To prevent stroke, one should avoid smoking, keep high pressure under control, diabetic patients should take medicine regularly, keep free from anxiety and lead a normal life.
---"}]

Reflex action means a sudden response or automatic reaction. Suddenly a needle pricks in the hand or on touching a hot object we immediately turn off hand from the source of stimulation. This is the result of reflex action. We cannot control the reflex action according to the will. Basically, it is controlled by the spinal cord, not by the brain. That is the immediate response to a specific stimulus is not controlled by the spinal cord instead of the brain is called reflex action. For example, a needle prick in the hand while sewing in an unconscious way or carelessly may cause a sudden jerking away of the hand. That is a reflex action. The events in such a reflex action are described in this way. At the time of pricking the dendrites of the sensory neuron, skin accepts the stimulus. Skin acts as a receptor. This stimulus transmits from the finger to the grey matter of the spinal cord through the axon of the neuron. It is the motor or efferent neurons which transmit impulses from the spinal cord to the dendrite of motor neuron. Here impulse is transmitted from the axon of the sensory neuron located at the grey matter of the spinal cord to the dendrite of the motor nerve by electrochemical process. Impulse transmits between the axon of the sensory nerve and dendrite of the motor or efferent nerve through the synapse. Then, the impulse from the dendrite impulse ultimately reaches the muscles and the muscles contract according to the command of the central nervous system. So, the hand is turned off from the source of stimulation automatically. Thus, sudden response is controlled by the spinal cord."}]
